🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICAN CONSUMER CONFIDENCE HITS 12-MONTH HIGH</u>

Consumer confidence climbed to 46.1 points in August — up a full point and its highest in a year, breaking a long run of annual declines, INEGI and Banxico reported. All five components rose, led by households' willingness to buy durable goods, while expectations of higher prices eased, across a survey of 2,336 urban homes. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MORENA TO US CHAMBER: RESPECT MEXICO'S SELF-RULE</u>

After Larry Rubin, head of the American Society of Mexico, called it a "grave error" to bar dual nationals from elected office, Morena's Citlalli Hernández reminded him whose call it is: "decisions about who can hold public office belong exclusively to the people of Mexico." Her mirror — the US Constitution reserves its presidency for natural-born citizens; imagine a foreign voice branding that "a grave error." "My position is respect for the self-determination of peoples."

🌧️🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO ROLLS OUT NATIONAL CLIMATE-ALERT SYSTEM</u>

Ahead of El Niño's floods and storms, Sheinbaum's government is installing command centers nationwide — focused on the Pacific — plus a new phone-alert system to warn communities before disaster hits, run through the military's DN-III-E and Plan Marina. "The plans already exist," Sheinbaum said, "but we set out how and when to inform the population, the shelters, everything there has to be." The strategy also maps crop shifts as heat reshapes farming like Sonora's wheat.

🔎🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S SEARCH STRATEGY LOCATES 13,625 MISSING</u>

Mexico's federal search strategy has located 13,625 missing people since July 2025 — 6,939 through the Single Identity Platform and 2,572 via the National Search Alert — part of 31,946 found since October 2024, the Interior Ministry reported. Undersecretary Arturo Medina Padilla says the 10-point plan now guarantees every case "a responsible authority, forensic experts, and a formal search plan."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM: LET CONGRESS PROBE FAR-RIGHT MEDDLING</u>

Sheinbaum says it "wouldn't be excessive" for Congress to investigate whether Argentine operative Fernando Cerimedo — bankrolled in Mexico by tycoon Ricardo Salinas Pliego — used paid bots and his outlet La Derecha Diario to manufacture public opinion ahead of 2027. Cerimedo and partner Javier Negre have openly boasted of swaying elections across the region; Chile's Congress already opened a commission, and Bolivia found a bot farm tied to him.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>111 OFFICIALS JAILED FOR CARTEL TIES: ZERO IMPUNITY</u>

Since Sheinbaum took office, 111 public officials — sitting mayors among them — have been arrested for organized-crime links, security chief Omar García Harfuch reported in the Second Government Report. It's part of 67,253 detentions for high-impact crimes, alongside 34,353 firearms seized — 80% of them trafficked in from the United States. Harfuch: "zero tolerance for corruption and zero impunity, whatever the position or party."

🇲🇽💵 <u>Remittances to Mexico rose again in July — $5.57 billion, six straight months up</u>

Banxico reports Mexican families received $5,571 million dollars in July, up 3% year-on-year and a sixth consecutive monthly increase, for $36.35 billion in the first seven months of 2026 (+3.1%), per El Financiero. It came from 13.1 million transactions averaging $426 each — and it held up despite Washington's aggressive deportation drive, with the very migrants the US targets sending more money home than a year ago.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexican forces dismantle 3 meth superlabs in Guerrero — even Washington's ambassador took notice</u>

Federal forces knocked out three methamphetamine labs in Guerrero, seizing tons of precursor chemicals and dozens of industrial-scale tanks in simultaneous raids. US Ambassador Ronald Johnson called it "otro ejemplo de lo que podemos lograr cuando nuestros países comparten información y se coordinan" — worth remembering that those precursors ship in from abroad, and the labs were taken down on Mexican soil by Mexican forces. Cooperation, not subordination.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Two ex-admirals ran one of Mexico's biggest fuel-smuggling networks, FGR confirms</u>

Attorney General Ernestina Godoy confirmed that brothers Roberto and Fernando Farías Laguna — both retired navy admirals — headed a "huachicol fiscal" operation moving fuel out of Texas mislabeled as "oil or additives" to dodge taxes, with 10 million liters of diesel seized from a single ship in Altamira and cells across five states. "Quien haya usado un uniforme, cargo público o aduana para servir al crimen, debe responder ante la justicia," she said. The case broke from an internal navy complaint — the institution turning on its own corruption.

🇲🇽💜 <u>42 million Mexicans now receive a pension or welfare program — over 1 trillion pesos a year</u>

Bienestar Secretary Leticia Ramírez Amaya put it plainly: "La riqueza de México debe traducirse en bienestar para el pueblo." 42 million people are covered — 13 million elderly on the universal pension alone (6,400 pesos every two months), plus women aged 60-64, people with disabilities, and 445,000 farmers under Sembrando Vida. This is what the 1 trillion pesos the opposition dismisses as "populism" actually buys.
